name: Courtallam Border Rahmath Parotta Stall
area: Tamil Nadu-Kerala border, near Sengottai (Tenkasi district)
signature_dish: Coin parotta with country chicken (naatukozhi) curry, served on banana leaf
why_it_matters: A legendary border eatery — Mohammad Hassan set it up in 1974 as a tent at the Tamil Nadu-Kerala border where toll stalls once stood. 'Courtallam Border parotta' is now a celebrated dish across the south; the stall has served celebrities and President APJ Abdul Kalam. The signature coin parotta with country-chicken curry, all on banana leaf, makes it the headline food stop for anyone visiting Courtallam Falls.
insider_tip: It is at the TN-Kerala border near Sengottai, a short drive from Courtallam — a destination stop, not a town eatery. Order the coin parotta with naatukozhi (country chicken) pepper. Mostly non-veg; busy with travellers and truckers, so go off-peak.
signature_address: Courtallam Border Rahmath Kadai, TN-Kerala border, Sengottai, Tenkasi District, Tamil Nadu 627809

name: Rahamath Barotta Stall
signature_dish: Soft barotta with spicy kuzhambu and naatukozhi pepper chicken
why_it_matters: A barotta stall in Courtallam itself — one of only a handful of restaurants Tripadvisor lists for the falls town — known for soft, flaky parotta and spicy non-veg, especially naatukozhi (country chicken) pepper. The everyday parotta-and-curry stop right by the falls.
insider_tip: Carries the Courtallam parotta tradition into the town itself. It is essentially a non-veg parotta stall — the only veg items are onion raita and water, and even the parotta uses egg. Naatukozhi pepper is the order.
signature_address: Rahamath Barotta Stall, Courtallam, Tenkasi District, Tamil Nadu 627802

name: Hotel Tamil Nadu Courtallam Restaurant (TTDC)
area: Tenkasi Road, opposite Sri Parasakthi College, Courtallam
signature_dish: Tamil unlimited meals on banana leaf at the state tourism hotel
why_it_matters: The restaurant of TTDC's Hotel Tamil Nadu at Courtallam — reviewers single it out as one of the most reliable, hygienic places to eat in a falls town where private restaurants are thin and inconsistent. A dependable Tamil meals stop close to the main falls.
insider_tip: In a town with limited dining, the TTDC restaurant is the safe, hygienic choice for a Tamil meal. On Tenkasi Road opposite Sri Parasakthi College; the unlimited meals at lunch are the order.
signature_address: Hotel Tamil Nadu Courtallam, 51E Tenkasi Road, opposite Sri Parasakthi College, Courtallam, Tamil Nadu 627802

name: Sri Madhuram Pure Vegetarian Restaurant
signature_dish: Pure-veg South Indian meals and tiffin on the Courtallam-Tenkasi road
why_it_matters: A pure-veg restaurant on the Courtallam-Tenkasi road — described as the best vegetarian option in the area. In a stretch dominated by non-veg parotta stalls, this is the reliable choice for a vegetarian thali or tiffin between Courtallam Falls and Tenkasi town.
insider_tip: On the road linking Courtallam to Tenkasi — easy to fold into the drive. This is the pure-veg counterpoint to the area's parotta stalls; go at lunch for the veg meals.
signature_address: Sri Madhuram Pure Vegetarian Restaurant, Courtallam-Tenkasi Road, near Tenkasi, Tenkasi District, Tamil Nadu 627811

name: Sri Balaji Bhavan (Tenkasi)
signature_dish: Pure-veg South Indian meals and tiffin in Tenkasi town
why_it_matters: A pure-veg restaurant in Tenkasi town — the nearest sizeable town to Courtallam, 6km away. Described as the best vegetarian option in Tenkasi, it is the reliable veg meals address for Courtallam visitors basing in or passing through Tenkasi.
insider_tip: Tenkasi is 6km from Courtallam Falls and has more dining choice than the falls town itself. Sri Balaji Bhavan is the veg pick — go at lunch for the meals, mornings for tiffin.
signature_address: Sri Balaji Bhavan, Tenkasi town, Tenkasi District, Tamil Nadu 627811
